expectations.text: States the Commission Q&A position (December 17, 2025): DORA applies to third-country branches in the EU if the home-country entity would qualify as an Art. 2 financial entity
expectations.evidence: No Commission Q&A of 17 Dec 2025; scope reasoned from CRD authorization and flagged as 'a genuinely debated area' with 'ongoing clarifications'.

expectations.text: Cites the Luxembourg operationalisation: CSSF's August 27, 2026 package — new Circular CSSF 26/915
expectations.evidence: 'I can't confirm a specific named CSSF circular... that took effect in August 2026'; CSSF 26/915 never cited, only speculative candidates.

expectations.text: Describes the effect: third-country branches removed from the legacy ICT/outsourcing circulars (20/750, 22/806) and brought into the DORA circular suite (including 25/882 on ICT third-party use and 25/893 on incident reporting)
expectations.evidence: No removal from 20/750/22/806, no 25/882/25/893, no DORA circular suite; effect of the August 2026 change not described.

expectations.text: Advises the practical consequence: the branch runs DORA-grade ICT risk management, third-party registers and incident reporting like an EU-incorporated entity
expectations.evidence: 'treat the branch as fully in scope', branch-level ICT risk framework, Register of Information entries, 'Incident reporting obligations run to the CSSF'.

expectations.text: Notes supervisory expectations are NCA-specific — verify the equivalent position with the relevant regulator in other member states
expectations.evidence: Notes NCA clarifications exist and CSSF's position, but never advises verifying the equivalent position with regulators in other member states.
